Nicole Marvin expressed frustration at the lack of gluten-free options in her local Aldi store after it ended a trial program offering these products. Nikki Williams, another Money reader, worries that rising energy costs will further increase food prices, making it difficult for people with dietary restrictions to afford their needs.

articles.title: LIC, HAL, among 10 stocks that saw sharpest decrease in government shareholding in Q4. Check list - Government Stakes Shrink | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: During the March 2026 quarter, the Government of India saw a significant decline in the value of its holdings across several major listed companies.  The value of LIC’s holding dropped by Rs 78,889 crore, while Indian Railway Finance Corp, Hindustan Aeronautics, and Bharat Petroleum Corporation also experienced substantial declines. The government's holdings in IDBI Bank, Punjab National Bank, Canara Bank, Rail Vikas Nigam, and Bank of Baroda also saw significant reductions.

articles.title: Rupee depreciation: What are the implications for commodities and Indian economy? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Rupee has weakened sharply due to factors like high import dependence on crude oil, widening trade deficits, and foreign portfolio outflows. This is further exacerbated by geopolitical tensions in West Asia, leading to higher oil prices and increased capital flight towards US assets. The weakening INR has a direct inflationary impact on commodities, pushing up import costs for essential goods. While the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has intervened in the forex market to stabilize the currency, sustained weakness remains a concern for the Indian economy.

articles.title: Why a flexible asset allocation approach beats static exposure over the next 3 years: ICICI Pru AMC’s Ihab Dalwai - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The fund manager of the Active Asset Allocator Long-Short strategy, a Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) framework, believes investors should avoid focusing on single asset classes and instead adopt a dynamic allocation approach.  They highlight that equities have become more attractive after recent corrections, while fixed income has gained prominence due to rising interest rates. The manager emphasizes the importance of monitoring growth trends, inflation, liquidity conditions, real interest rates, currency movements, and earnings cycles when making investment decisions. They also suggest that InvITs can play a diversification role within portfolios but acknowledge potential valuation pressure in a rising rate environment.  The fund manager believes midcaps offer selective opportunities but cautions against overpaying for certain sectors.

articles.title: NSE extends equity F&O segment timings till 3:40 pm from August - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) announced changes to its derivatives segment trading hours and closing price calculation methodology. Trading will begin at 9:00 am and end at 4:15 pm, with the pre-open session ending at 9:08 am. The volume-weighted average price will continue to be used for closing prices, calculated based on trades executed during the last half hour of trading (3:10 pm to 3:40 pm).  The exchange will also cancel unexecuted special orders and pending orders outside the revised price band.

articles.title: Vizhinjam seaport in Kerala becomes fastest Indian port to handle 2 million TEUs cargo in 18 months - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vizhinjam International Seaport in Kerala has achieved a significant milestone by handling 20 lakh TEUs of cargo in just 18 months, nearly twice its annual capacity. The port, developed and operated by Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd. (APSEZ) for the Kerala government, is now the first Indian port to achieve this feat.  The port's strategic location along the Indian Ocean corridor and deep draft capabilities make it a competitive transshipment destination in the region, attracting large container vessels like MSC Irina and MSC Verona. Vizhinjam is also expected to handle more cargo with its second phase expansion, which will be completed by 2028.

articles.title: Sebi imposes penalty on Suzlon, executives for misstating financials - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has overturned an earlier decision that exonerated Suzlon and its executives. The regulator will now impose penalties after initiating an investigation in 2019 based on an anonymous complaint alleging irregularities in the company's dealings. Sebi claims that Suzlon improperly valued a business sale, concealed significant liabilities, and misclassified financial obligations, leading to inflated profits and capital raising.

articles.title: Gold demand drops 70% after sharp duty hike in India - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India's gold import demand fell to about 7.5 tonnes in the fortnight ended May 27, a significant drop from around 25 tonnes a year earlier. The government increased the import duty on gold to 15% from 6%, leading to a 70% decline in demand according to industry estimates. Joyalukkas, a gold jewellery retail chain, reported a 35% drop in demand.  The World Gold Council (WGC) noted that while large chain stores saw a brief period of panic buying, mid-sized and regional jewellers are continuing to see demand from affluent customers but are expected to rely more on gold exchange programs going forward.

articles.title: Pakistani freelancers outearn regional rivals - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's freelancers earned over $950 million in foreign exchange during the first 10 months of fiscal year 2026, a 49% increase from the previous year.  Dr Imran Batada, president and CEO of the Pakistan Freelancers Association (PFA), attributed this growth to increased participation on platforms like Upwork and Fiverr, as well as rising awareness among Pakistanis about freelancing opportunities. The PFA is working to organize training sessions for freelancers in emerging trends and payment processes.

articles.title: RBI efforts boost rupee usage, yet global adoption remains limited - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has implemented measures to encourage the use of the rupee in cross-border trade. These include allowing correspondent banks in partner countries to open Special Rupee Vostro Accounts with Indian banks and facilitating local currency settlement arrangements with several nations. This initiative aims to support India's ambition of becoming a developed economy, as previously stated by former RBI Deputy Governor T Rabi Sankar.

articles.title: MSCI index rejig, US-Iran deal worries spook Dalal Street - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The NSE Nifty and BSE Sensex closed lower on Friday, reflecting a sell-off triggered by the MSCI rebalancing.  Foreign portfolio investors sold shares worth ₹21,105.9 crore, while domestic institutional investors bought shares worth ₹16,764.1 crore. The indices were impacted by the addition of several companies to the MSCI Standard Index and concerns over the US-Iran nuclear deal. Despite the volatility, analysts remain optimistic about the broader market's resilience.

articles.title: Govt mulls scrapping export tax in budget - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan government is considering a one percent advance tax removal on exporters as part of limited, targeted measures in the upcoming federal budget. The textile sector, which accounts for the bulk of Pakistan's exports, has proposed a range of reforms including the restoration of the Final Tax Regime (FTR), reduction in energy tariffs, and clearance of over Rs327bn in pending refunds. However, these demands are unlikely to be accommodated due to revenue targets and ongoing stabilization commitments. The textile sector argues that Pakistan faces an estimated 68.27 percent tax burden, exceeding regional competitors, which hinders export competitiveness.

articles.title: Government defends Farmer Discom proposal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Rural Power Distribution Company Limited (TGRPDCL) Chairman and Managing Director Musharraf Ali Faruqui stated that no metering would be introduced for agricultural consumers under the proposed Farmer Discom model. The TGRPDCL argued that existing discoms in Telangana are financially stressed, with accumulated losses reaching ₹69,741 crore by FY 2025, and operational inefficiencies contribute to high AT&C losses of 19.84% in FY 2025. The proposed model aims to improve electricity distribution and reliability for farmers while focusing on improving service quality and reducing technical and commercial losses.

articles.title: A.P. Chambers seeks Vande Bharat services to more destinations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry Federation (AP Chambers) president Potluri Bhaskara Rao requested South Coast Railway Zone General Manager Sandip Mathur to increase train frequency from Vijayawada to major destinations, including Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Cochin. He also urged the expansion of Vande Bharat services and dedicated freight corridors for industrial growth and logistics efficiency in the state.

articles.title: Dedicated policy framework proposed for Sivakasi’s ₹6,000-crore fireworks industry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S. Keerthana, Minister for Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce, proposed a new policy framework for the fireworks industry in Sivakasi during an internal meeting with officials from the Industries and Guidance Departments. The policy aims to formalize the sector by addressing worker safety, welfare, factory owner concerns, and other issues. Activists and labor groups are calling for improvements in safety standards for women workers handling hazardous chemicals, humane working conditions across factories, and the elimination of illegal units.  The new government is expected to address these concerns as well as the impact of the Supreme Court's ban on barium nitrate and support for export opportunities.

articles.title: Canada dips into technical recession? Pierre Poilievre slams Mark Carney, says no other G7 country is in this situation - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Canada entered a technical recession after reporting two consecutive quarters of economic contraction, according to Statistics Canada. The first quarter saw real gross domestic product fall 0.1 per cent on an annualized basis, following a downwardly revised contraction of one percent in the fourth quarter of 2025.  Opposition leader Pierre Poilievre criticized Prime Minister Mark Carney, stating that he is the only G7 leader to have led his country into a recession. Economists, however, are debating whether this situation can be definitively classified as a technical recession due to the small dip in the first quarter and potential for revision.  The Bank of Canada projects growth at 1.2 percent for this year.

articles.title: Kerala start-up unveils first AI system-on-chip - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Netrasemi, a semiconductor start-up based in Thiruvananthapuram, India, announced the successful completion of silicon bring-up for its flagship AI system-on-chip (SoC), A2000. The company plans to begin volume production of the chip at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company in Taiwan next year and aims to help global platform developers bring advanced AI algorithms to small edge devices.  The A2000, one of India's first AI/ML chips, features proprietary hardware acceleration IPs and a heterogeneous graph-stream parallel processing architecture designed for compact, power- and cost-sensitive edge devices. The company received ₹15 crore in DLI support from the Central government and has raised ₹125 crore in funding.

articles.title: War & AImpact: China's export-price jump fastest in 3 years - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Global export prices rose 5% in April, the largest increase since April 2023, driven by increases in commodities like crude oil, metals, and semiconductors. Chinese goods prices, however, continue to fall due to intense domestic competition and oversupply, with China's factories absorbing much of the raw material price spike. This shift could pose challenges for international consumers as it may lead to higher prices for consumer items.

articles.title: NA, Senate budget sessions summoned on June 5 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari has summoned separate sessions of the National Assembly and the Senate on June 5 to announce the federal budget for the fiscal year (FY) 2026-27. The meetings of the Annual Plan Coordination Committee (APCC) and the National Economic Council (NEC), which review economic performance and set targets, are scheduled in the first week of June.  The government is expected to present the budget to parliament in the second week of June.  The IMF concluded its visit to Pakistan last week, focusing on the "budget strategy" for the next fiscal year.

articles.title: Notification on blending isobutanol with diesel this year: Road secretary V Umashankar - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Secretary Umashankar of the Indian Ministry of Road Transport and Highways stated that blending of diesel is likely to begin later this year due to its significant impact on energy security. The CII Knight Frank Report, released at a summit, highlighted India's progress in logistics cost reduction, with investments reaching nearly $360 billion over the past decade.  The report also emphasized the need for more multi-modal logistics parks (MMLPs) to achieve optimal efficiency and support freight modal shift towards rail and other efficient modes of transport.

articles.title: RBI to explore CBDC pilot in cross-border transactions - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) plans to expand the use of its Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) in cross-border transactions and domestic retail space during the current fiscal year. The RBI signed a memorandum of understanding with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) for digital asset collaboration and held discussions with the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) for operationalizing a cross-border CBDC pilot.  The central bank also joined multilateral BIS-Innovation Hub-led initiatives to enhance cross-border payments through CBDCs. The value of bank notes in circulation in digital form, CBDC-R, decreased from Rs 1,016.46 crore to Rs 771.66 crore during the fiscal year.

articles.title: India, Canada launch trade & investment forum - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Goyal, during his recent trade missions to Canada and the United States, emphasized the importance of enhancing connectivity and fostering business partnerships. He met with Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu, business leaders in both countries, and prominent figures like Ted Pick (Morgan Stanley) and Chip Kaye (Warburg Pincus).  These engagements focused on expanding trade, investment, innovation, and supply chain collaborations to drive shared prosperity between the nations.

articles.title: Supreme Court sets aside 'fraud' findings, disgorgement of ₹447 crore in 2007 RPL Futures Trading case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court overturned findings of fraud against Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in connection with RIL's futures trading of November 2007. The court ruled that the SEBI's use of the "PFUTP Regulations" to determine fraud was flawed, stating that the threshold for 'fraud' under these regulations is high and the market regulator used an incorrect method for calculating RIL's share of the market.  The court also ordered the refund of ₹250 crore deposited in the Investor’s Protection Fund by RIL.

articles.title: US stocks today: US stocks hits new closing highs on tech strength, Middle East deal hopes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all rose on Thursday, driven by strong earnings growth and optimism surrounding artificial intelligence.  Wells Fargo's chief equity strategist Ohsung Kwon advised investors to buy and hold AI stocks while selling call options for additional income. The rally was fueled by renewed optimism around AI and strong earnings growth, despite concerns about inflation and the global economy.  The S&P 500 communications services sector, however, declined due to a drop in Alphabet shares.

articles.title: 'If you do it badly...': JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon confronts Zohran Mamdani during closed-door meeting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, met with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani to discuss key issues affecting New Yorkers, including affordable housing and childcare.  Dimon cautioned against poorly designed policies, emphasizing the importance of expertise and proper implementation. He also criticized politicians who focus on taxes and spending rather than fixing systems and administration. Dimon expressed his willingness to assist if the city pursues practical solutions. The meeting took place on May 18th, following Mamdani's separate meetings with David Solomon, CEO of Goldman Sachs.

articles.title: Moody's upgrades Reliance Industries rating to Baa1, now 2 notches above India's sovereign rating - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Reliance Industries has been upgraded two notches above India's sovereign rating by both Moody's and S&P Global Ratings, reflecting its strong credit profile and diversified business operations. The ratings agency cited Reliance's counter-cyclical business segments, international exposure, and financial discipline as key factors supporting the upgrade. However, Moody's maintained a two-notch cap on the rating due to Reliance's significant linkages to the domestic economy through its retail and digital businesses.  The stable outlook reflects expectations for continued earnings growth across most of its business segments.

articles.title: Social Security payment change will affect 3.6 million beneficiaries: What Direct Express users need to know | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of the Treasury is transitioning the Direct Express prepaid debit card program from Comerica Bank to Fifth Third Bank, affecting an estimated 3.6 million cardholders. The change will involve replacing existing cards with new ones issued by Fifth Third Bank.  Beneficiaries should continue receiving their benefits normally and can expect advance notice before receiving a replacement card.

articles.title: Dell shares soar more than 30% on strong earnings - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dell, a leading PC manufacturer, saw its AI server revenue soar to $16.1 billion in the recent quarter, surpassing its traditional PC business and contributing significantly to the company's increased market value of $206 billion. Analysts praised Dell's strong execution and argued it is the best way to play in the AI market.  The company's focus on AI servers and infrastructure solutions has outperformed its PC business, while also benefiting from strong demand for CPU racks from AI cloud providers like CoreWeave and Nscale.

articles.title: Will the AI race fuel another boom or another bubble? | Technology | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic are preparing for public listings, potentially creating one of the largest tech IPO waves in history. The companies' combined valuations already exceed trillions of dollars, with investors including pension funds and retirement savings potentially owning shares without their consent. These firms require substantial capital to develop data centers, servers, and infrastructure, prompting them to seek funding through public offerings. However, none of the companies have yet generated annual profits, and analysts caution about the opacity of their business models.

articles.title: Sebi eases nomination rules for demat accounts, mutual funds. Check full details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the market regulator, has revised rules regarding nominations for single-holder demat accounts and mutual fund folios. The new framework mandates nomination for single-holder accounts unless investors opt out, while jointly held accounts will have an optional nomination process.  The regulator also simplified the nomination process by removing the need for a witness signature when using a regular signature.  These changes aim to improve ease of investing and reduce unclaimed assets after investor death. The new rules will come into effect on September 1, 2026.

articles.title: Govt cuts petrol, diesel prices by Rs22 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) announced a reduction of Rs22 per litre in the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) on Friday. The price reductions follow last week's cuts, bringing the new HSD price to around Rs380 per litre and petrol to around Rs381 per litre. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that providing relief to the people is his top priority, emphasizing the government's commitment to passing on fuel subsidy benefits to various sectors. The Petroleum Division confirmed the new prices will be effective starting May 30th.

articles.title: Vedanta shares jump 2% to hit fresh 52-week high. What’s behind the surge? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta's shares reached a 52-week high on Friday, following an upgrade from ICRA, which removed the company from watch with developing implications.  ICRA upgraded Vedanta's long-term rating to AA+ (Stable), citing strong financial risk profile and expected continued healthy operating performance. The ratings agency also expects the group to continue supporting dividend requirements through intra-group support, further strengthening its credit profile.

articles.title: Multibaggers: 15 stocks with 25%+ sales and profit growth in Q4 March 2026 - ​Growth Drives Multibaggers | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A recent analysis by ETMarkets.com identified 124 non-financial companies with high sales and profit growth in the March 2026 quarter, resulting in a significant increase in stock prices for many of these firms.  The top 15 stocks that gained between 125% and 615% over the past year include Sterlite Technologies, MTAR Technologies, CIAN Agro Industries & Infrastructure, Bajaj Consumer Care, Bliss GVS Pharma, TD Power Systems, Apollo Micro Systems, Acutaas Chemicals, Quality Power Electrical Equipments, Precision Wires India, Kwality Pharmaceuticals, Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys, Sansera Engineering, GE Vernova T&D India, and Hindustan Copper.  These companies demonstrate strong financial performance, supporting sustained gains in stock prices.

articles.title: Nomura downgrades Cummins India shares to Neutral despite raising target price by 25%. Here’s why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Cummins India reported a 23% increase in total sales for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, driven by domestic sales growth. Nomura, however, lowered its target price on the stock to 49x FY28 estimated earnings due to near-term gross margin headwinds from commodity inflation. The brokerage anticipates strong growth in the data center segment and the Distribution segment, but expects margin pressure to continue through the first half of FY27.

articles.title: HFCL shares soar 17% in two days, rally 170% in 2026. Should you buy, sell or hold? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HFCL received a significant purchase order worth Rs 135.09 crore from RailTel Corporation of India for the annual maintenance contract (AMC) of its Secure Operations (OPS) Network project, which involves setting up a secure defence communication network. The company's revenue nearly doubled year-over-year to Rs 1,824 crore in the March quarter, with EBITDA swinging from negative territory to Rs 315 crore and PAT moving from a loss of Rs 83 crore to a profit of Rs 184 crore. Analysts believe that HFCL's diversification into defence and aerospace through its Defsys subsidiary, data centre interconnect solutions, and the growing AI market will drive future growth.

articles.title: Ola Electric shares jump 9%, skyrocket 93% in 2 months. What's fuelling the rally? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ola Electric shares surged to a high of Rs 42.88 on the NSE Friday, marking their highest point since January 7th this year. The stock has rebounded significantly from its all-time low of Rs 22.25 in March. While the company reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 500 crore for Q4 FY26, down 42.5% from the previous year, Ola Electric saw sequential volume improvement and market share gains. Emkay attributes this to increased production capacity, price-sensitive market share, and competition from other players like Ather.

articles.title: Netweb Technologies jumps 15%, hits fresh 52-week high after rating upgrade - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Netweb Technologies, a company offering computing solutions, is celebrating a ratings upgrade from CRISIL Ratings Limited. The rating agency has upgraded the company's long-term rating to 'Crisil A+ / Stable' and reaffirmed its short-term rating to Crisil A1.  CRISIL believes sustained revenue growth and efficient working capital management will support Netweb Technologies' continued financial health, while caveats include potential declines in revenue or operating margin that could negatively impact net cash accruals.

articles.title: Ashok Leyland shares fall 2% after Q4 results. Do Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley see any upside? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Leyland's fourth quarter revenue grew over 17% year-on-year to Rs 17,417 crore.  Analysts at Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Motilal Oswal maintained their ratings on the company with varying price targets.  While near-term demand is expected to be driven by mining, infrastructure tippers, and tractor trailers, analysts caution against short-term margin pressure due to commodity inflation and rising diesel prices.

articles.title: HDFC Bank shares fall 5% in two sessions; lender responds to recent Rs 45 crore differential payment report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HDFC Bank issued a statement clarifying that its internal audit function routinely reviews practices and addresses any observations. The bank maintains sound financial practices and robust internal controls, stating it remains committed to corporate governance and regulatory compliance.  The report in The Indian Express stated that an internal audit flagged payments made to the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) just days before former chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned on March 18th. The bank's Chief Marketing Officer, Ravi Santhanam, acknowledged the marketing department facilitated a "camouflage" of interest reimbursement as marketing spend during senior-level discussions.  The Vigilance probe report was sent to two top committees: the Audit Committee and the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.

articles.title: Silver drops Rs 1,500/kg, gold at Rs 1.56 lakh/10 gms as Iran war tensions weigh. Key levels to watch - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX silver futures for July 2026 delivery fell by Rs 1,518 to Rs 2,68,018 per kg, while gold futures for June 2026 delivery dropped by Rs 609 to Rs 1,56,316 per 10 grams. U.S. inflation accelerated in April, prompting economists to expect the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates unchanged for a prolonged period.  John Williams, President of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, stated that monetary policy remains appropriately positioned given the current economic outlook and predicted elevated inflation in the near term before easing later this year.

articles.title: Coal India OFS gets good demand amid green energy risks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Coal India Ltd (CIL)'s Initial Public Offering (IPO) saw strong demand from non-retail investors, leading to a 8.14 times subscription on the first day. The government exercised its greenshoe option, extending the offering period. However, some analysts remain skeptical about the long-term investment case for CIL, citing concerns over global and domestic energy transition towards cleaner sources.  The stock closed 1.2% higher at ₹463.60 on Wednesday with a floor price of ₹412, translating to a discount of about 9.6%.

articles.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks rise on US-Iran truce deal, oil drops - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.7% on Friday, fueled by optimism toward artificial intelligence and a potential ceasefire extension in the Iran-Saudi Arabia conflict. Dell Technologies Inc. surged after strong sales outlook, while Brent crude prices fell slightly.  The yen remained steady against the dollar, with US Treasury yields falling across the curve. Despite concerns about inflation, investors remain optimistic about a resolution to the Iran conflict and continued growth in the tech sector.

articles.title: Listed banks earned a record profit of ₹4 lakh crore in FY26 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Private banks and state-run banks both reported increased profits in the fiscal year 2026, with consolidated net profit rising 4.5% to ₹4.11 lakh crore.  The banking industry's overall growth was impacted by a rise in government bond yields and a cap on net open positions, which weighed on treasury income. SBI Chairman S C Setty noted that the economic fallout of the West Asia crisis may lead to lower GDP growth and higher inflation in FY2027, impacting credit growth.  Loan growth is expected to expand by 13%-15% in FY27, with private and PSU banks reporting almost equal profits despite PSU banks holding a larger market share.

articles.title: Ace investors take a hit on portfolios in March quarter - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hemendra Kothari and Mukul Agrawal suffered significant losses in their portfolios, with holdings dropping over 25% during the quarter.  Madhusudan Kela saw a 21% decline in his portfolio, according to data from primeinfobase.com. The portfolios of the late Rakesh Jhunjhunwala's family and Anil Kumar Goel experienced minimal impact.

articles.title: Labour poised for fresh welfare changes after scale of youth jobs crisis revealed | UK unemployment and employment statistics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alan Milburn, former Labour cabinet minister, released a report highlighting the significant economic cost of youth unemployment in Britain. The report estimated that youth unemployment costs the UK economy over £125 billion annually and called for a "whole system reset" involving schools, welfare, and employers to address this crisis. Keir Starmer's government has pledged to tackle youth unemployment by investing in a "youth guarantee" and funding more work experience placements. While some opposition leaders and business groups criticize Labour's policies, the government is taking steps to address the issue, including an increase in funding for employment support programs.

articles.title: Why investors are ready to play in global equity league - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian investors are increasingly looking to invest overseas due to strong global market performance, particularly in AI and semiconductors.  Three main avenues exist: international mutual funds offered by Indian fund houses, GIFT City-based funds, and direct investing through international brokerage accounts. However, the Reserve Bank of India has imposed a $7 billion limit on overseas investments, restricting access for many investors.

articles.title: ‘Hundreds of job applications’: young people on their struggle to find work | Unemployment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Young people in the UK are facing significant challenges finding work, with many struggling to secure permanent positions despite actively seeking employment. Catherina, Olivia, and Giovanna all cite difficulties finding jobs due to a competitive market, lack of support from employers, and limited opportunities for career development.  These young individuals have sought help from organizations like Spear, the Young Women’s Trust, and the Drive Forward Foundation. They highlight the need for greater government guidance on disability rights and employer obligations, as well as improved access to training and financial support.

articles.title: US inflation surges to three-year high amid tensions with Iran | Inflation News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US inflation surged to a three-year high in April, driven by heightened energy prices due to tensions with Iran. Personal consumption expenditures rose 3.8 percent year-over-year, marking the fastest pace since early 2020.  The increase was fueled by a 5.5 percent jump in petrol prices and a 0.5 percent rise in food costs. The Federal Reserve faces pressure to address rising inflation ahead of its upcoming policy meeting. Despite the report, US markets remained positive.

articles.title: ‘Hidden datacentre tax’ costing Irish households millions, report says | Computing | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ireland’s growing number of datacentres has significantly increased household electricity bills, according to a report commissioned by Friends of the Earth Ireland and Beyond Fossil Fuels. The report found that datacentres consumed 22% of the country's electricity last year, more than all urban homes combined, and drained €715 million from the Irish economy.  The report argues this "hidden data centre tax" on household bills could lead to further price increases in the future. Industry representatives dispute these findings, claiming datacentres boost the economy and are already meeting high renewable energy standards.

articles.title: Ministers visit paddy procurement centre, ask officials to speed up purchase - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, the Minister for Civil Supplies and Irrigation of Telangana, visited procurement centers to assess damage caused by recent unseasonal rains on paddy stock.  He assured farmers that the government would continue procuring paddy without disruption and ensure they receive the Minimum Support Price (MSP). The government has procured 58 lakh tonnes of paddy so far and expects another 18 lakh tonnes to arrive in the coming days. Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy also instructed officials to intensify lifting operations, improve storage arrangements, and strengthen coordination between departments to prevent delays in transportation.

articles.title: New food exports deal signals end to Brexit ‘sausage wars’ | Brexit | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK and EU have reached an agreement on new food exports rules, eliminating paperwork and physical checks for certain products from the summer of 2027. The deal will significantly ease burdens on businesses selling to Northern Ireland and reduce costs for exporters.  The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs published guidance to help producers prepare for the changes, which include easing requirements for food additives, colorings, animal breeding certificates, pesticides, vaccination residues, organic products, and farm feeds. The agreement is expected to boost the economy by £5.1 billion annually and support British jobs.

articles.title: Burberry boss could earn up to £12.2m under new bonus scheme as company rolls back climate goals | Burberry group | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Burberry's new bonus scheme for its CEO, Joshua Schulman, could earn him up to £12.2 million, while the company has scaled back its climate goals.  Schulman's pay package increased significantly, reflecting a focus on reviving sales and reducing costs. The company reported pre-tax profits of £49 million, driven by efforts to win back Chinese and North American shoppers under Schulman's Burberry Forward campaign. However, Burberry has pushed back its deadline to become carbon neutral by a decade to 2050, aligning with other major companies that have adjusted their climate targets in recent years.

articles.title: US stocks today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit record closing highs as US and Iran agree to extend ceasefire - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's approval is needed for negotiations on Iran's nuclear program to proceed during the truce period. Despite rising inflation and a slower economic growth, the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all experienced gains. Investor confidence remains high as they anticipate continued resilience in the global economy and corporate earnings despite geopolitical instability.  The market is optimistic about the long-term investment case for AI and other sectors that could benefit from increased spending on cybersecurity, defense technology, energy infrastructure, and supply chain resiliency.

articles.title: ₹237 crore per acre land deal near Raidurg shatters records - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Limited (TGIIC) auctioned a 6.29-acre land parcel for ₹237 crore per acre, setting a new benchmark in the city's real estate market. The final bid price was 70.5% higher than the reserve price and attracted intense bidding from national realty players. MSTC platform facilitated the e-auction, while JLL acted as the transaction advisor.  The overall deal value is approximately ₹1,490.73 crore.

articles.title: Ashok Leyland Q4 Results: Net profit rises 14% to Rs 1,291 crore, firm announces Rs 2.5 interim dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Leyland reported a 17% year-over-year increase in revenue to Rs 17,417 crore for the fourth quarter of its fiscal year ending March 31, 2026. The company's total expenses rose over 18% YoY to Rs 15,493 crore during the same period. Ashok Leyland announced a second interim dividend of Rs 2.5 per share for the financial year 2026.  The record date for determining eligibility is June 3rd and there will be no final dividend for the year. The company's Chairman, Dheeraj Hinduja, attributed the record-breaking performance to innovation, customer satisfaction, and global market expansion.

articles.title: Bharat Dynamics Q4 Results: Net profit tumbles 59% to Rs 113 crore; dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bharat Dynamics (BDL) reported a significant decline in revenue and net profit for the fiscal year 2026. Revenue fell by 27% year-over-year to Rs 2,442 crore while net profit dropped 23% to Rs 420 crore. Total expenses also decreased to Rs 2,298 crore during the year. The company's board of directors recommended a final dividend of Rs 0.40 per equity share with a face value of Rs 5 each, subject to shareholder approval at its upcoming AGM.

articles.title: Bharti Airtel, HAL, among 7 stocks that have upside potential of up 28%. Do you own any? - Bluechip bets | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ICICI Securities has identified seven large-cap Indian stocks with potential for significant upside, citing strong fundamentals and long-term growth prospects. The firm's picks include Larsen & Toubro, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Hindustan Aeronautics, Asian Paints, Power Finance Corporation, Mahindra & Mahindra, and Bharti Airtel.  These companies offer a range of potential upside, with the highest projected gain at 28% for Mahindra & Mahindra and the lowest at 15% for Asian Paints.

articles.title: Commodity upcycle: Why copper and aluminium could explode in coming quarters. Should Indians invest? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Commodity metals, including copper and aluminum, are experiencing a surge in demand driven by factors like electrification, AI development, and defense spending.  HDFC Securities, Morgan Stanley, and other analysts predict these metals will outperform US equities in the near future due to structural supply shortages and geopolitical disruptions. The S&P GSCI-to-S&P 500 ratio is at a historically low level, suggesting that commodity prices are undervalued relative to stocks.  MCX Metals have seen significant price increases, with analysts recommending a "buy on dips" strategy for investors seeking long-term gains.

articles.title: Dolly Khanna’s portfolio sees steady gains in CY26; 5 stocks rise up to 25% - Portfolio Moves | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dolly Khanna, an ace investor, saw her portfolio increase in value by 8% to approximately Rs 481 crore as of May 27, 2026.  Five stocks within her portfolio gained between 4% and 26%, while three declined between 15% and 22%. Khanna added three new stocks during the March 2026 quarter, including Chennai Petroleum Corporation, Rain Industries, and Sharda Cropchem. The value of these additions totaled approximately Rs 379 crore.

articles.title: Top 4 debt mutual fund managers oversee over Rs 1 lakh crore AUM in March quarter.Check details - AUM wise | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ventura, ETMarkets.com, and other sources report that the top four debt mutual fund managers in India manage at least Rs 1 lakh crore of assets under management (AUM) as of March 2026 quarter. Kaustubh Gupta of Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund leads with Rs 1.61 lakh crore AUM, followed by Manish Banthia of ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund with Rs 1.45 lakh crore AUM.  Deepak Agrawal of Kotak Mutual Fund manages Rs 1.29 lakh crore AUM and Rajeev Radhakrishnan of SBI Mutual Fund has Rs 1.14 lakh crore AUM.

articles.title: Bitcoin trades at $73K amid US-Iran tensions; ETF outflows top $2.5 billion in 2 weeks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The cryptocurrency market experienced a downturn, with Bitcoin falling below $74,000 and Ethereum dropping to near $1,977.  CoinDCX Research Team reported over $700 million in liquidations, primarily driven by geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran and concerns about institutional flows. Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus, emphasized the importance of reclaiming the $80,000 mark for market stability.  Avinash Shekhar, Co-Founder & CEO of Pi42, advised investors to adopt a long-term approach and remain patient during periods of volatility.

articles.title: Smallcap IPOs dominated MF portfolios in March quarter. Which stocks made the top 10? - New entrants | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ventura reports that mutual fund portfolios heavily invested in smallcap IPOs during the March quarter. The top 10 companies with market values exceeding Rs 20 crore, according to the report, include Amagi Media Labs, Fractal Analytics, Sedemac Mechatronics, Shadowfax Technologies, CMPDI, Omnitech Engineering, Powerica, Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions, Bharat Coking Coal, and AYE Finance.

articles.title: Greener pasture of a shepherd’s life lures Chinese workers penned in by ‘996’ jobs | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Chinese farm owner's recruitment drive for shepherds, seeking to fill two positions on his Inner Mongolia ranch, attracted over 700 applicants from diverse backgrounds, including recent university graduates and factory workers. The high salary of 8,000 yuan per month, along with provided accommodation and groceries, drew interest from individuals struggling to find work in China's competitive job market, where unemployment rates remain a concern. Despite the initial success, Zuo Xiaoyong, the farm owner, has decided to prioritize experienced shepherds for future roles due to the challenging working conditions on his ranch.

articles.title: Nifty Midcap 100 scales fresh peak, analysts see more upside ahead - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty Midcap 100 index rose 0.4% on Wednesday, reaching a new high, driven by strong earnings visibility and growth outlook in the midcap sector.  Analysts predict further gains of 20% in the medium term as domestic-focused sectors like defense, power, and industrials continue to attract investor interest. SBI Securities and Religare Broking highlight that most stocks in the index are trading above their long-term averages, with many reaching fresh highs.

articles.title: Santos says it won’t ‘exert any effort’ on Narrabri gas project while it focuses on Beetaloo Basin | Santos | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Santos chief executive, Kevin Gallagher, announced the company will not invest in its Narrabri gas project while awaiting outstanding approvals.  Gallagher stated that the company is prioritizing exploration in the Beetaloo Basin and will re-evaluate domestic assets after appraising Beetaloo reserves. This decision has prompted concerns from opponents of the project, including Georgina Woods of Lock the Gate, who argue it prolongs stress for communities defending the land and water resources.  Independent MP Roy Butler questioned Premier Chris Minns about the delay, asking if the government acknowledges the Narrabri gasfields are smaller than expected and high in carbon dioxide, which contradicts climate change policies. Minns defended the need for gas production to support manufacturing and energy needs while emphasizing the state's commitment to renewable energy investments.

articles.title: Fuel price hike: Schools in Bengaluru plan to increase transport fee - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Private schools in Bengaluru are planning to increase transport fees by 8% to 10% this academic year due to rising fuel prices.  The Associated Management of English Medium Schools in Karnataka, and the Karnataka Recognised Unaided Private School Association (KRUPA), have both announced plans for fee increases after conducting meetings with parents. Some parents expressed concerns about the added financial burden on their budgets, while others are considering alternative transportation options like BMTC buses if fees increase further.

articles.title: BIS organises awareness session for footwear manufacturers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) organized an awareness session for footwear manufacturers in Ambur, Tirupattur. The event aimed to educate MSMEs and stakeholders on Indian Standards, Quality Control Orders, conformity assessment, and testing requirements.  Senior BIS officials from Chennai participated alongside representatives from Vellore and Ranipet leather industry clusters.

articles.title: From $642 to $4 million: Fired JPMorgan employee wins huge compensation over food platter dispute - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A former JPMorgan Chase broker, Brent Ryan Bodner, was awarded $4 million in damages by a Wall Street arbitration panel after claiming he was wrongfully fired over a $642.50 deli platter for a business meeting. The ruling ordered JPMorgan Chase to pay Bodner the compensation and also recommended correcting his employment record.  The bank has not yet decided whether it will appeal the decision.

articles.title: Markets rally amid hopes of US-Iran deal | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Markets rallied on Wednesday as hopes for a US-Iran deal increased, fueled by reports of potential concessions from Iran. The rally was driven by speculation that the deal would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ease global economic uncertainty.  However, despite initial optimism, the White House dismissed the report as a fabrication, and key sticking points remain unresolved, including Iran's nuclear infrastructure and ballistic missile program.

articles.title: The world's carmakers are struggling to compete with China
articles.rephrased_article: Chinese carmakers are rapidly gaining ground in the global market, outpacing Western brands in areas like electric vehicles, batteries, and software development.  Foreign carmakers, including Tesla, BMW, and General Motors, are adjusting their partnerships with Chinese companies to remain competitive.  These changes include joint ventures for production and technology sharing, as well as the expansion of Chinese-designed vehicles into international markets.  While some Western brands like Toyota, Hyundai, and Ford are expanding research operations in China, others face challenges such as declining sales and heavy discounts on their models. The shift in manufacturing power is raising concerns about job losses and economic impact in Southeast Asia and Europe.

articles.title: Number of Neets in UK could hit 1.25m by early 2030s, Milburn review will say | Work & careers | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alan Milburn, former Labour health secretary, warns that Britain risks a 25% rise in young people not in work or education by the early 2030s without urgent government action. His report, commissioned by Pat McFadden, will argue that overhauling health and disability benefits for young people is crucial to addressing youth unemployment.  Milburn calls for a "reset" of the system, highlighting its failure to enable participation in the labor market and arguing that current policies are exacerbating inactivity. The report also criticizes employers and the government for failing to provide adequate entry-level jobs and opportunities.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow posts closing record high, S&P 500, Nasdaq muted as AI rally pauses - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Banking stocks declined as JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned of increased expenses, while the White House denied reports of Iran restoring Strait of Hormuz shipping. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose, driven by healthcare and consumer stocks, but tech shares fell after reaching record highs. The S&P 500 gained slightly, with energy and chip stocks experiencing declines.  Analysts suggest that market momentum is stretched while the Federal Reserve's key inflation measure will provide further insight into monetary policy.

articles.title: Lifting of internet restrictions reveals Iranians’ anger over food inflation | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian authorities partially restored internet access after a three-month suspension, revealing widespread anger over soaring food prices.  The Ministry of Intelligence expressed concerns about the potential for "cognitive warfare" and warned against using internet freedom to incite protests. While President Masoud Pezeshkian blamed the US for Iran's economic woes, support for continuing internet restrictions was low at 9%. The government launched a resistance economy committee to address price gouging and shortages, but hyperinflation remains endemic in the country.  Some citizens expressed relief at regaining global connectivity while others criticized the government's attempts to control online discourse.

articles.title: DGGI set to fire up GST recovery drive against gaming firms after Supreme Court's backing - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has ruled in favor of the DGGI, validating their tax demands against approximately 80 online gaming companies and casinos.  The court's decision allows for an aggressive recovery process, following show-cause notices alleging tax evasion of around ₹1 lakh crore. The revenue department will now study the ruling and is open to engaging with industry stakeholders regarding penalties and interest. This verdict is expected to impact major gaming companies like Gameskraft, Dream11, Mobile Premier League, Games24x7, Junglee Games, and Delta Corp.

articles.title: Tomato, onion and flour rates surge - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Consumers are facing rising prices for essential items like onions, tomatoes, and flour ahead of Eidul Azha. Haji Shahjahan, President of the Falahi Anjuman Wholesale Vegetable Market, attributes the price hikes to low onion and tomato arrivals from Sindh and Balochistan, as well as increased demand.  Waheed Ahmed, Patron-in-Chief of the All Pakistan Fruit and Vegetable Exporters, Importers and Merchants Association, reports a sharp decline in vegetable exports due to the closure of the Afghan border and the US-Israel war on Iran. Flour prices have also risen due to higher wheat prices in the open market.

articles.title: Funds sanctioned to three corporations towards property tax dues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana government has approved a ₹1,686.39 crore One Time Settlement (OTS) scheme for settling long-pending property tax arrears on government properties in Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, Cyberabad Municipal Corporation, and Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation. The scheme offers a 100% waiver on accumulated interest and penalties, with the government clearing the arrears through installments within one year.  The Finance Department released budget orders for the amount on May 26th.

articles.title: Will the AI race fuel another boom or another bubble? | Technology | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic are preparing for public listings, potentially marking a significant wave of tech company offerings.  These firms, valued in the trillions, aim to raise capital through these listings to fund their data center and server infrastructure needs. However, none have yet generated annual profits, and analysts express concerns about the transparency of their business models.

articles.title: Bangladesh seeks IMF aid: How badly has Iran war hit its economy? | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh has requested a new IMF-supported program to address the economic fallout of the US-Israel war on Iran. The country's energy crisis, caused by disruptions in oil and natural gas supplies, has led to rising fuel prices and impacts on industries like garment manufacturing.  The IMF remains committed to supporting Bangladesh's efforts for macroeconomic stability and financial resilience. The request comes as Bangladesh grapples with a growing debt burden exacerbated by the war.

articles.title: Zydus Lifesciences buyback alert! Last date to buy shares to participate in Rs 1,100 crore buyback at 7% premium - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Zydus Lifesciences announced a share buyback program, with the record date set for May 29th. The company will buy back up to 95.65 lakh shares at a price of Rs 1,150 each, representing 0.95% of its paid-up equity share capital.  The buyback is expected to be conducted via the tender route and investors must buy shares by May 27th to ensure eligibility for the program. The company's board has also recommended a final dividend of Re 1 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the Annual General Meeting scheduled for August 11th.

articles.title: Hindalco, Nalco shares jump up to 5% after aluminium prices hit 4-year high. Where is metal headed? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hindalco and Nalco saw significant gains on the BSE, driven by rising aluminum prices on the London Metal Exchange.  The increase in prices is attributed to concerns about Chinese aluminum smelter production cuts as the country tightens energy consumption and emissions regulations. Morgan Stanley analysts predict strong demand for aluminum, supported by a tighter supply-demand balance, despite potential downside risks from global growth deterioration. They also initiated coverage with an 'Overweight' rating on Hindalco, forecasting a potential upside of over 20% from the previous closing price.

articles.title: Samsung memory chip staff in line for £310,000 bonuses after AI profit-sharing deal | Samsung | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Samsung Electronics employees in its memory chip division will receive average bonuses of £310,000 each as a result of a profit-sharing agreement with the South Korean government. The deal, which averts a potential strike, sets aside 10.5% of operating profits for bonus payments to workers. This agreement comes amid a surge in demand for memory chips from AI datacenters, driving up prices and boosting profits for chipmakers like SK Hynix and Micron, whose stock values have surpassed $1 trillion.

articles.title: Coal India shares drop 6% after OFS launch. Buy the dip or wait? Here’s what technical indicators suggest - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Coal India's share price dropped to Rs 428.40 on Wednesday, marking the sharpest single-day fall since June 2024. The government will offer 1% of its equity capital for sale, with an oversubscription option to sell an additional 2%.  The floor price is set at Rs 412 per share, potentially raising more than Rs 5,000 crore. Analysts believe the stock's near-term chart is cautious but not structurally broken and will react to the supply event.

articles.title: Finolex Industries shares jump 8% after Q4 profit surges 59% YoY; stock rallies 20% in a week - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Finolex Industries reported a significant increase in net profit and revenue for the March quarter, with a 59% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 261 crore.  Revenue from operations rose 12% YoY to Rs 1,314 crore, driven by improved realizations. The company's full-year performance, however, remained under pressure with a 25% decline in net profit to Rs 599 crore compared to FY25. Despite this, the board recommended a final dividend of Rs 2 per equity share along with a special dividend of Rs 0.75 per share, subject to shareholder approval. The stock has seen strong buying interest recently and is trading above all 8 key simple moving averages, signaling sustained upward momentum.

articles.title: JP Power shares soar 20% on optimism around Adani Power’s 24% stake purchase - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Power announced agreements to acquire a 24% stake in Jaiprakash Associates Limited’s (JAL) JPVL and the Churk thermal power plant for approximately Rs 2,993.6 crore and Rs 1,200 crore respectively. The acquisitions are part of the broader Adani Group-led resolution plan for debt-laden JAL and will strengthen Adani Power’s generation portfolio and expand its footprint in the thermal power sector.  The transactions are expected to close within 90 days from the NCLT approval granted on March 17, 2026. This comes as India experiences a heatwave amid an exceptionally strong El Niño year, leading to increased power demand.

articles.title: Market Wrap: Sensex falls 142 points, Nifty holds 23,900; HDFC Bank shares tumble 3% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex closed down 142 points at 75,868 while the Nifty 50 fell 7 points to end the session at 23,907.  HDFC Bank shares were the top losers on the Sensex, falling nearly 3% after a report on an internal probe over Rs 45 crore interest payments spooked investors.  However, Power Grid shares gained nearly 3%.  India VIX fell 6% to 15.24.  Foreign investors remained net sellers of Indian equities on Tuesday, selling shares worth Rs 2,408 crore. Oil prices remained below the crucial $100 per barrel mark.

articles.title: Gina Rinehart bankrolls purchase of 10% stake in Seven network owner Southern Cross Media | Gina Rinehart | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gina Rinehart, Australia’s richest person, has provided a loan to Bruce McWilliam for his acquisition of a nearly 10% stake in Southern Cross Media, which owns the Seven Network and other media brands. The investment, worth approximately $26 million, gives Rinehart significant influence over the company's future despite not directly owning shares.  This move marks Rinehart’s return to the media industry after a previous foray into the sector with Ten Network and Fairfax Media.

articles.title: HDFC Bank shares fall 2% on reports of internal probe over Rs 45 cr interest payments - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HDFC Bank allegedly routed differential interest payments to the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC), a state government agency, through its marketing department disguised as road safety awareness campaign sponsorship. This practice violated RBI regulations and the bank's own anti-bribery policy. The bank’s former chairman, Atanu Chakraborty, resigned on March 18th citing ethical concerns related to these practices.  The bank's share prices have declined significantly since the resignation.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged abuse of power and violation of regulations by a major bank raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Adani Power surpasses Infosys in market capitalisation after 126% rally in one year - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Power's stock surged to become India's 11th most valued company, driven by soaring power demand fueled by the intense El Niño year and heatwave conditions.  The surge comes as India grapples with record-breaking temperatures, placing it among the world's hottest cities. Infosys, meanwhile, saw its share price decline due to concerns about the impact of AI advancements on the software-as-a-service market.

articles.title: Taiwan’s economy is booming thanks to AI. Not everyone sees the benefits | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Taiwan's economy is experiencing rapid growth due to its semiconductor industry, which powers leading AI models.  However, this boom has raised concerns about wealth inequality and the uneven distribution of benefits. While the stock market has seen significant gains, many Taiwanese workers in non-tech sectors are facing rising costs for housing and living expenses. The Central Bank Governor Yang Chin-lung has sounded the alarm about an "K-shaped economy," where certain sectors grow rapidly while others stagnate.  Some argue that Taiwan's economic model is becoming too reliant on a single industry, leaving other sectors behind.

articles.title: Supreme Court sets aside NCLAT order which rejected Amazon's appeal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court overturned the decisions of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) and the Competition Commission of India (CCI) regarding Amazon's investment deal with Future Group. The court ruled that the NCLAT and CCI orders, which had rejected Amazon's appeal and levied a penalty on it, were invalid.  The Supreme Court ordered the refund of any amounts deposited or recovered from Amazon based on these orders within eight weeks.

articles.title: LIC shares drop 4% on Rs 10,000 crore govt stake sale buzz - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The government plans to sell a 2% stake in the state-run insurer, Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), to institutional investors in late June or early July.  The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) is working with financial institutions including Goldman Sachs Group, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, BNP Paribas SA, and IIFL Capital Services to manage the transaction. LIC has been given until May 2032 to meet regulatory requirements for a minimum public shareholding of 25%.  The insurer recently announced its first-ever bonus issue in a ratio of 1:1.

articles.title: Top gold loan companies expand bullion holdings to record levels in FY26 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India's gold imports fell by nearly 5% year-on-year to 721 tonnes in FY26, according to commerce ministry data.  IIFL Finance saw its gold holdings rise due to regulatory action lifting restrictions on the company's gold loan business. Muthoot Finance saw a decline in gold holdings, while Manappuram Finance reported a record high in gold holdings.
